purpose: ASVS V1.3.3 had no decision. It asks that data reaching a potentially dangerous context is sanitized first - only characters that are safe for the context, and input that is too long trimmed. The web tier takes four client-controlled header values and puts them back into an outgoing HTTP request header: x-correlation-id (40 reads), idempotency-key (8), user-agent (13) and the client address chain (10 routes). None restricted characters; 51 of the 63 reads did not bound length either.
requiredInvariants: No header injection is claimed, because there is none. Measured on Node 22: new Headers() refuses only NUL, CR, LF and code points above U+00FF, and header bytes off the wire are decoded as latin1, so a wire-delivered value can never reach that last case. CR and LF cannot reach a handler at all - the HTTP parser ends the field there. What the runtime does forward verbatim is every other C0 control character, DEL, and the whole 0x80-0xFF range, at any length. That is the gap this closes.

My first hypothesis was wrong and was corrected by experiment, not argument. I expected a high-byte header to make the route throw; a real http server fed raw 0xD0 0xAF over a socket showed the value arriving as latin1 code points 208 and 175 and the Headers constructor accepting it. The range was then mapped one code point at a time rather than guessed.

The allowlist is the codebase's own. [A-Za-z0-9._:-] with a 128-character bound is exactly CORRELATION_PATTERN and IDEMPOTENCY_PATTERN in organization-connect/route.ts, the strictest public surface here. Every identifier the product generates is inside it - randomUUID, the SHA-256 hex markers the staff review queue builds, and the decision:/org-join-decision: keys the API builds.

Checked before choosing it: buildPlatformV7IdempotencyKey normalizes with [^a-z0-9а-яё_-], so a platform-v7 key can contain Cyrillic. An ASCII allowlist would have silently altered such a key and broken idempotency. It never travels as a header - execution-envelope-helper puts it in a request body field - and every header-borne key in the product is ASCII. Traced rather than assumed.

organization-connect was left alone. It validates with an anchored pattern instead of repairing, which is the right shape for a public surface, and routing it through a sanitizer would have let a value that fails the pattern become one that passes after unsafe characters are stripped.

The guard found two sites the greps missed - raw x-forwarded-for reads in organization-connect and gekta-auth-route. Both turned out to be stricter than anything else here: they take the nearest hop and validate it, with the reason written next to them.

Recorded, not changed: ten routes select the leftmost X-Forwarded-For entry, which the caller writes, while those two select the nearest hop because REG.RU production terminates at one trusted edge. The API resolves the chain against trusted CIDRs (trusted-proxy.ts), so the leftmost selection hands it a caller-chosen rate-limit bucket. Which selection is right depends on what terminates each surface, and nearest-hop behind a CDN would collapse every user into one bucket, so the two policies are now named side by side in one module instead of being unified on a guess. Sanitizing a value and deciding whose value to believe are different questions; this requirement is the first.

One deliberate behaviour change in the address chain: it now yields the first value that is an address rather than the first that is non-empty, so a junk header no longer hides a usable one after it. A second: the two nearest-hop routes used node:net isIP and echoed the spelling given, so one address written two ways was two rate-limit buckets; safeClientIp canonicalizes. Both are tested.

Two prior chain orders (cf-connecting-ip first, and x-nf-client-connection-ip first on the two login routes) are unified on the longer order. They differ only when two CDN headers are set on one request.
39 now-unused randomUUID imports were removed rather than left behind.
No production, REG.RU, DNS or database mutation. No registration business logic, 1C, marketing or presentation change.

Two existing tests asserted this logic by scanning source and broke when it moved. Both were re-bound across the halves rather than relaxed: the anti-abuse test now requires the public surface to call the nearest-hop function AND that function to still take the nearest hop and validate it, keeping every negative assertion and adding one that the weaker chain is not used there; the staff-proxy test now requires the sanitizing read. Each was re-falsified three ways - pointing the surface at the weaker chain, stripping nearest-hop out of the module, and restoring the raw read - and each fails again.
acceptance: node scripts/security/verify-forwarded-header-sanitization.mjs exits 0: 2 remaining raw reads, 1 sanitized at the read, 1 validated by an anchored pattern, 0 unaccounted for.

vitest run tests/unit/forwardedHeaderSanitization.spec.ts: 23 passed, 0 failed. The file is pinned to the node environment - the default happy-dom Headers refuses nothing, so the runtime boundary asserted there would otherwise have measured the test environment.

ASVS V1.3.3 moves NOT_ASSESSED to PASS: PASS 129 to 130, NOT_ASSESSED 39 to 38, FAIL and NOT_APPLICABLE unchanged, rejected decisions back to the single pre-existing V8.2.4. No other decision's conditions were broken by the refactor.
Revocable: widening the identifier allowlist rejects V1.3.3; dropping the guard's anchored-pattern requirement rejects V1.3.3.
